blocks.content: Before we dive into reversing the linked list, let's grasp the concept of sliding references.
Sliding references refer to a technique where multiple references move together, allowing us to traverse and manipulate linked list nodes efficiently.
In our example, we'll use three pointers: prev_node, current, and next_node. Initially, these references will be positioned as follows:
Initially we'll set current pointer to the head node and next_node to its succeeding node.

Node<T>* current = head;
Node<T>* next_node = current->next;
As there's no element before the head node, we'll initially set prev_node to nullptr.
We'll then set each of the pointers to point to the succeeding node of the node they currently point to.
Since multiple references slide or move together in a coordinated manner; they are called sliding references.
Now we will use this concept to reverse a linked list.
